sessions.title: Introduction to HTML
choices: It specifies the character encoding of the document.
It declares the document type and version of HTML.
It sets the title of the web page.
It defines the root element of the HTML document.
sessions.content:
HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) is the standard markup language used to create web pages. HTML documents are made up of elements, which are represented by tags. Here’s a basic structure of an HTML document: ```html My First Web Page

Welcome to My Web Page

This is my first paragraph.

``` - ``: Declares the document type and version of HTML. - ``: The root element of the HTML document. - ``: Contains meta-information about the document, such as the title. - ``: Sets the title of the web page, which appears in the browser tab. - `<body>`: Contains the content of the web page. - `<h1>`: A heading element, with `h1` being the highest level. - `<p>`: A paragraph element.
sessions.exercise: Create a simple HTML document with a title, a heading, and a paragraph. Save it as `index.html` and open it in a web browser to see the result.
sessions.question: What is the purpose of the `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration in an HTML document?
sessions.objective: Understand the basics of HTML and how to create a simple web page.

sessions.title: HTML Elements and Attributes
sessions.content:
HTML elements are the building blocks of a web page. Each element has a start tag, content, and an end tag. Attributes provide additional information about an element and are added to the start tag. Here’s an example of an anchor element with an attribute: ```html Visit Example ``` - ``: The anchor element is used to create hyperlinks. - `href`: An attribute that specifies the URL of the page the link goes to. Other common attributes include: - `class`: Used to specify a class for an element, which can be used in CSS for styling. - `id`: Used to specify a unique identifier for an element. - `src`: Used in image elements to specify the source of the image. Example of using `class` and `id`: ```html

This is a paragraph inside a div with a class and an id.

```
sessions.exercise: Create an HTML document with a `div` element that has a `class` and an `id` attribute. Inside the `div`, add a paragraph and a link to an external website.
sessions.question: Which attribute is used to specify the URL of a hyperlink in an anchor element?
sessions.objective: Learn about HTML elements and how to use attributes to modify their behavior.

sessions.title: HTML Lists
sessions.content:
HTML provides three types of lists: ordered lists, unordered lists, and description lists. Ordered lists are used for items that need to be in a specific order, while unordered lists are used for items that do not need to be in a specific order. Description lists are used to describe terms or names. Here’s an example of each: - Ordered List: ```html
  1. First item
  2. Second item
  3. Third item
``` - Unordered List: ```html
  • First item
  • Second item
  • Third item
``` - Description List: ```html
Term 1
Description of Term 1
Term 2
Description of Term 2
``` - `

    • `: List item element. - `

sessions.objective: Learn how to create and use different types of HTML lists.
